chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman in exchange for a room in his house, and he had partners in that house. He said: 'It is permissible for him and for her, and there is no pre-emption (shuf'ah) for any of the partners against her.'

key_terms.شُفْعَة: Pre-emption (right of first refusal to buy out a co-owner's share)

ai.seo_question: Do co-owners have the right of pre-emption when a man marries a woman by giving her a room in his co-owned house?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that in a marriage contract (Mahr) involving a share of co-owned real estate, the wife acquires her specific portion directly, thereby excluding the general right of pre-emption (Shuf'ah) that typically applies to co-owners in sales. This ruling highlights the distinction between a transfer of ownership via marriage settlement versus a standard commercial sale, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding property rights and marital contracts. The hadith is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflecting the practical legal applications derived from the Imams during the period of the Major Occultation.
